subject: Created a shiny website with knitr

messages.author: a814dd0eade31e3e
messages.subject: Created a shiny website with knitr
parts:
I was able to create a multi-page website using Rmd files and knitr. See https://github.com/vnijs/shiny-site. Works great ... mostly.

One thing that doesn't quite work the way I would like is rendering a slider. See example Rmd file linked below. sliderInput generates HTML but is rendered as a textinput in the html page. A work-around is to define the slider in server.R and use uiOutput in the Rmd file. Not a big deal. Just curious why it happens and if there is perhaps a better work-around.

https://github.com/vnijs/shiny-site/blob/master/page2.Rmd

Just in case ... I do know you can use the shiny runtime with rmarkdown to create an interactive webpage but, afaik, this doesn't allow you to build a multi-page website.

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Created a shiny website with knitr
parts:
My guess is that it is because you were using knitr::knit2html() (R
Markdown v1) to compile the Rmd documents, and R Markdown v1 does not
understand HTML dependencies. A slider is initially a text input, and
the JS library turns the text input into a slider. R Markdown v1 is
not aware of the JS dependency attached on sliderInput(), so the
slider is not rendered.

Regards,
Yihui
--
Yihui Xie <xiey...@gmail.com>

I'm looking at the documentation for rmarkdown::run with multiple pages (http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com/authoring_shiny_advanced.html#multiple-pages) but it is not clear to me if this could be used to create a multi-page site with a navbar.
